headline: Local geometry and graph topology inform single-cell dynamics inference
label: Geometric Context In Cell Dynamics
summary: Geometry-aware flow matching and topology-based models now tie spatial context to single-cell trajectories, fate, and perturbation response.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is the use of explicit geometric or topological context to model single-cell states along trajectories. LoCoFlow couples local point-cloud geometry with conditional fate uncertainty for trajectory and fate inference, while GeoSinkhorn Flow applies geometry-aware flow matching under perturbation conditioning to turn static phenoscapes into dynamic ones. MGCBRL encodes multiscale graph topology through nonlinear Burgers dynamics to produce response descriptors for protein B-factor prediction and single-cell type classification. What appears new is direct coupling of local geometry to dynamical or fate inference. BLOOM and JuloVelo extend flow and velocity modeling with biological priors, but they do not foreground geometry. Signal Associa maps field-spanning NK cell coupling networks, and the astrocyte transformer study reports predictability limits in trajectory forecasting.
